name: Wavesy AI Summary Links
author: Wavesy

sections.description:
Your readers already use AI assistants to make sense of what they read. Wavesy AI Summary Links puts a clean “AI Summary” row on your posts so they can open your article in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Grok in one click — with a prompt you write, pointing back to your page.

No API keys. No AI bills. No chatbot slowing down your site. The plugin simply builds smart, pre-filled links, so it stays fast and free forever.

Built and maintained by the content and CRO team at Wavesy.

Why publishers use it

  • Keep readers engaged with your content – instead of copy-pasting your text somewhere else, readers get a summary that cites and links back to your page.
  • Get your brand in front of AI – every click sends your URL, title and site name into the assistant, helping your content get associated with your brand where people now search and research.
  • You control the message – write the prompt once (“Summarize this article from {site_name} and list the key takeaways…”) and every summary starts from your framing.
  • Zero cost, zero maintenance – nothing runs on your server and there are no tokens to pay for or keys to rotate.
  • Looks native on any theme – a compact, accessible row that matches your design, with brand-colored icons or a single color of your choice.

Features

Works with the AI tools your readers use

  • ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Grok out of the box
  • Add your own providers (any AI tool that accepts a query in the URL)
  • Swap in your own icon artwork by replacing the SVG files

Prompts you control

  • Customizable prompt template with smart placeholders: {url}, {title}, {site_name}, {domain}, {description}
  • Ready-made presets to get started in seconds
  • Pulls your meta description from Yoast SEO, Rank Math or All in One SEO when available

Place it anywhere

  • Automatic placement above or below post content
  • Floating bar on the left or right side of the screen
  • Choose which post types show it, and exclude specific posts
  • Gutenberg block, shortcode [wavesy_ai_summary_links] and classic widget
  • Native elements for Elementor, Bricks and Breakdance

Make it yours

  • Per-provider brand colors or one custom color
  • Adjustable icon and button sizes and spacing
  • Card or transparent style to blend into any layout
  • Custom label text (e.g. “AI Summary:”, “Ask AI about this post:”)

Extra tools for content teams

  • Google Preferred Sources button (optional) – invite readers to add your site as a preferred source in Google
  • Written summary box in the post editor – generate a summary with your favorite AI, paste it in and save it with the post
  • AI-agent ready – on WordPress 6.9+, MCP-compatible agents can read post context and save summaries via the WordPress Abilities API

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open Settings → Wavesy AI Summary Links and pick a prompt preset (or write your own).
  3. Choose where the row appears – automatically, as a floating bar, or with the block/shortcode.
  4. Readers click an AI icon and get an instant summary of your page in the assistant they prefer.

About Wavesy

Wavesy is a conversion-focused agency helping brands turn traffic into revenue through CRO, content and experimentation. We built Wavesy AI Summary Links for our own clients’ content and made it free for everyone.

  • Website: wavesy.io
  • Need help growing conversions? Talk to Wavesy

The plugin is free software under the GPLv2 or later and independent of any AI vendor.

External services

When a visitor clicks an AI provider button, their browser opens that provider’s website with your configured query. Data sent depends on your template (typically page URL, title, and site name). Review each provider’s terms and privacy policy:

  • OpenAI / ChatGPT — https://openai.com/policies
  • Anthropic / Claude — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google / Gemini — https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • Perplexity — https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/privacy-policy
  • xAI / Grok — https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy

If you enable Google Preferred Sources, the plugin loads https://news.google.com/swg/js/v1/publisher.js on pages where the widget appears. See Google Preferred Sources documentation.

Privacy

This plugin does not run analytics or send visitor data to Wavesy. It stores settings in your WordPress database and optional per-post written summaries in post meta. Outbound requests occur only when a visitor clicks a provider link (their browser opens that service) or when Google Preferred Sources is enabled (Google’s script loads on pages that display the widget). No tracking pixels or hidden phone-home behavior are included.

Trademarks

ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, Google, and related marks are trademarks of their respective owners. Wavesy AI Summary Links is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with or endorsed by those companies.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install from the WordPress.org directory.
  2. Activate Wavesy AI Summary Links.
  3. Go to Settings → Wavesy AI Summary Links (or Tools → AI Summary).
  4. Configure your query template, providers, and placement.
  5. Use the block, shortcode, widget, or automatic placement.
sections.faq:
Is this plugin free?

Yes. Wavesy AI Summary Links is free software under the GPLv2+ license, built by the Wavesy content team.

Does this plugin call OpenAI or other AI APIs?

No. It only creates links that open in the visitor’s browser.

Do I need API keys?

No.

Will it slow down my site?

No. There is no chatbot, iframe or AI script on your pages – just lightweight links and a small stylesheet. Google’s script loads only if you turn on the optional Preferred Sources button.

Who makes this plugin?

Wavesy AI Summary Links is built and maintained by Wavesy, a conversion-focused agency. Visit wavesy.io to learn more about our work.

Can I use my own provider logos?

Yes. Replace the SVG files in assets/icons/ (for example chatgpt.svg, claude.svg) with your own 24×24 (or square) SVGs. Keep the same filenames or add custom providers in settings.

How do I add the widget to a post?

Use the Wavesy AI Summary Links block, shortcode [wavesy_ai_summary_links], or enable automatic/floating placement in settings.

Where is the Bricks element?

In Bricks, open the element panel and search for Wavesy AI Summary Links (category General). Bricks must be active when the plugin loads; after updating the plugin, refresh the builder once.

Where is the Elementor widget?

In Elementor, search the widget panel for Wavesy AI Summary Links (category General).

Where is the Breakdance element?

In Breakdance, search the Add panel for Wavesy AI Summary Links (category Other). Requires Breakdance with Element Studio element loading. You can also use Breakdance’s Shortcode element with [wavesy_ai_summary_links].

Where is the Gutenberg block?

In the block editor, search for Wavesy AI Summary Links (category Widgets).
sections.changelog:
1.5.0

  • Renamed the plugin to Wavesy AI Summary Links with the approved slug and text domain.
  • Adopted the unique WASL_/wasl_ prefix across PHP, storage, hooks, assets, block, and integrations for WordPress.org reviewer compliance.
  • Preserved transparent styling, vertical floating placement, Google Preferred Sources rules, and builder integrations from 1.4.0.

1.3.9

  • Plugin Check fixes: escaping, Tested up to 7.1, PHPCS prefix config, admin PHP tags.

1.3.8

  • Widget theme Transparent (no background/border); icon spacing 8–12 px; floating column vertically centered; Google Preferred Sources hidden on floating placement.

1.3.7

  • Update default provider SVG logos (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok) in assets/icons/.

1.3.6

  • Register Elementor and Breakdance integrations on the correct hooks; ship a proper Breakdance Element Studio element with SSR.
  • Gutenberg block editor script dependencies registered explicitly.

1.3.5

  • Fix Bricks element registration timing so Wavesy AI Summary Links appears in the builder panel.
  • Release zip excludes developer docs and Markdown files (WordPress.org readme remains in readme.txt).

1.3.4

  • Load default provider artwork from bundled SVG files; remove circular icon borders; larger default icon size; WordPress.org readme updates.

1.3.3

  • Bricks content hooks for above/below placement; floating z-index default 9999999; late wp_footer output.

1.3.2

  • Branded icons, Grok, custom providers, icon/button size and color settings.

1.3.1

  • Fix settings page access; Tools → AI Summary menu.

1.3.0

  • Initial public release.
